title: Walt Disney Beats Estimates as Q4 Revenue Rises 16% to $25.9 Billion and Adjusted EPS Hits $1.77
excerpt: Streaming profit more than doubled, parks posted record results and ESPN rode record NFL viewership as Disney beat estimates, raised its dividend 33% and guided to double-digit earnings growth in fiscal 2027.
body:
• Walt Disney beat Wall Street estimates in fiscal Q4 2026: adjusted earnings of $1.77 per share, up 59% from $1.11 a year earlier and above the $1.67 LSEG consensus, on revenue up 16% to $25.95 billion.
  • All three segments grew: Entertainment revenue rose 17% to $11.89 billion, Experiences rose 15% to $10.10 billion and Sports rose 16% to $4.61 billion, lifting total segment operating income 43% to $4.97 billion.
  • Streaming turned more profitable: subscription video revenue rose 19% to $6.05 billion and streaming operating income more than doubled to $824 million from $402 million.
  • Disney raised its dividend 33% to $2.00 per share, guided to double-digit adjusted EPS growth in fiscal 2027, and targeted $3 billion in annual cost savings by fiscal 2029.

Walt Disney closed fiscal 2026 with a fourth quarter that beat Wall Street on both lines. The company reported revenue of $25.95 billion for the quarter ended October 3, up 16% from $22.46 billion a year earlier, and adjusted earnings of $1.77 per share, up from $1.11, according to its earnings release filed with the SEC. Analysts had expected $1.67 per share, according to LSEG data cited by Reuters, and $25.26 billion in revenue, according to Zacks. Diluted EPS rose to $1.51 from $0.73, and shares rose about 2% in early trading, Reuters reported.

An extra week flatters the comparisons

One qualifier runs through the quarter: fiscal 2026 had 53 weeks, one more than the prior year, and the extra week fell in the fourth quarter. Disney estimates it contributed about $0.17 to full-year adjusted earnings per share. Excluding it, full-year segment operating income still grew about 10% and adjusted EPS about 16%. For fiscal 2026 as a whole, revenue rose 8% to $102.34 billion, total segment operating income rose 12% to $19.73 billion and adjusted earnings per share rose 18% to $7.02.

Streaming and entertainment lead the beat

Entertainment was the largest contributor. Segment revenue rose 17% to $11.89 billion and operating income rose 92% to $1.33 billion, from $691 million a year earlier. Subscription video revenue rose 19% to $6.05 billion, and streaming operating income rose to $824 million from $402 million. Disney credited higher subscription fees, advertising and engagement, helped by Toy Story 5. It also said it will stop providing the supplemental streaming operating income disclosure from 2027.

"Fiscal 2026 was a defining year for The Walt Disney Company. At a moment of real change, we stayed focused on delivering for our fans, creating value for our shareholders, and building on the momentum of this extraordinary company."

— Josh D'Amaro, Chief Executive Officer, Walt Disney

Parks and sports set the pace on the ground

Experiences, the division that runs theme parks, resorts and cruises, reported revenue up 15% to $10.10 billion and operating income up 20% to $2.25 billion, which Reuters described as record revenue and profit for the unit. Disney said global guest numbers rose 4% excluding the extra week. Sports revenue rose 16% to $4.61 billion and operating income rose 53% to $1.39 billion, as ESPN viewership for the start of the NFL and college football seasons reached record highs, according to the company and Reuters.

Dividend up, content spending up, costs targeted down

Disney's board declared an annual dividend of $2.00 per share, up 33% from the $1.50 paid in fiscal 2026, payable in two $1.00 installments on January 22, 2027 and July 13, 2027. The company repurchased $9.0 billion of shares across the year, returning $11.6 billion to shareholders in total. Management also targeted about $3 billion in annual run-rate cost savings by fiscal 2029, with most savings to be reinvested, and said cash content spending will rise about 9% to about $26 billion in fiscal 2027, including more on sports rights and international programming.

For fiscal 2027, Disney expects double-digit growth in adjusted earnings per share, excluding the 53rd week it will lap in the fourth quarter, and total segment operating income growth of about 8% on the same basis. It expects about $5.4 billion of segment operating income in the first quarter, capital expenditures of about $9 billion, free cash flow of about $11 billion and share repurchases of about $9 billion.
